dossier.public_summary: The periodic dip lines up with the target star and looks flat-bottomed with no secondary eclipse. The period is essentially identical to the star's 1.01-day rotation, and the star shows a very large brightness swing at that period comparable to the transit depth. The dip depth appears twice as deep in one sector as another, as spots evolve. Together this is best explained as spot-induced modulation rather than a planet.

reasons.why: Difference imaging puts the dip on the target and excludes all plausible neighbours (closest suspect 45.9 sigma away), ruling out a neighbour eclipse.
Transit is flat-bottomed, not V-shaped, against a grazing stellar binary.
No secondary eclipse; an EB on target would show one for this period.

Period and large sinusoidal modulation match the star's rotation exactly, with modulation amplitude (6644 ppm phase_curve amplitude_ppm ratio_to_depth 1.017) comparable to the dip depth (6531 ppm), indicating spot activity.

Depth changes by 64% between sectors measured by the same source (TESS-SPOC). sector_depths_by_source verdict changes_within_a_source p_constant_all 1.0364767233733755e-13 shows the change is astrophysical and sector-specific, as expected for evolving starspots.
